title: Verify Next advances the carousel by exactly one slide
preconditions: Home page (/) is loaded on the target environment at desktop viewport 1280x800; user is not logged in
Featured Projects section is scrolled into view
Carousel is on the first slide
steps: Read the translate3d X offset of the slide track and the title of the first visible slide
Click the Next button (#carousel__next) once
Wait about 1 second for the slide animation to finish
Read the translate3d X offset and the title of the first visible slide again
expected_result: The track offset decreases by one slide step (about 891px, within tolerance) and the previously second slide becomes the first visible slide. The page URL does not change.

title: Verify Next on the last slide wraps back to the first slide
preconditions: Home page (/) is loaded on the target environment at desktop viewport 1280x800; user is not logged in
Featured Projects section is scrolled into view
Carousel is on the first slide

test_data.clicks_to_reach_last_slide: data-total - 1 (4 at the time of exploration)

steps: Click Next once, then wait about 1 second for the slide animation to finish; repeat until the last slide (item--4 for 5 slides) is the current slide (data-total - 1 clicks in total)
Read the translate3d X offset of the slide track
Click Next once more and wait about 1 second for the slide animation to finish
Read the translate3d X offset and the title of the first visible slide
expected_result: After the extra Next click the carousel wraps: the track returns to the initial (first slide) offset and the first slide is the first visible slide again.

title: Verify Prev moves back by exactly one slide after Next
preconditions: Home page (/) is loaded on the target environment at desktop viewport 1280x800; user is not logged in
Featured Projects section is scrolled into view
Carousel is on the first slide
steps: Click Next once and wait about 1 second for the slide animation to finish
Read the translate3d X offset (offset A)
Click Next once more and wait about 1 second for the slide animation to finish
Click the Prev button (#carousel__prev) once and wait about 1 second for the slide animation to finish
Read the translate3d X offset (offset B)
expected_result: Offset B equals offset A (within tolerance): Prev moves the carousel back by exactly one slide.

title: Verify Prev on the first slide does not move or wrap the carousel
preconditions: Home page (/) is loaded on the target environment at desktop viewport 1280x800; user is not logged in
Featured Projects section is scrolled into view
Carousel is on the first slide

test_data.note: asserts current behaviour; Prev does not wrap (see OPEN RISKS in explorer handoff)

steps: Read the translate3d X offset of the slide track and the title of the first visible slide
Click the Prev button (#carousel__prev) once
Wait about 1 second for the slide animation to finish
Read the translate3d X offset and the title of the first visible slide again
expected_result: Nothing changes: the track offset and the first visible slide are the same as before the click (no movement, no wrap to the last slide). No error is shown and the page does not navigate.

title: Verify rapid repeated Next clicks do not break the carousel
preconditions: Home page (/) is loaded on the target environment at desktop viewport 1280x800; user is not logged in
Featured Projects section is scrolled into view
Carousel is on the first slide
steps: Click the Next button (#carousel__next) 5 times in quick succession without waiting between clicks
Wait about 1 second for the slide animation to finish
Read the translate3d X offset of the slide track and check the browser console for uncaught errors
Click Next once more, wait about 1 second for the slide animation to finish, and read the offset again
expected_result: No uncaught JavaScript error is raised and all slides are still present. After the rapid clicks the track rests at a valid slide position (offset is 0 or a negative whole multiple of one slide step, within tolerance). The additional Next click still changes the track position.
